confirmed.title: Workbook re-import brings back Form-inbox cases the resident deleted, and duplicates ones whose date was fixed in the app or whose Form response was edited after pick-up
confirmed.scenario:
Three ways to hit it. In each one the sheet still holds the response row (no app: marker), because deletes and edits made in the app never reach the sheet.
(a) A resident sends a case through the Google Form, and the inbox brings it into the app as a 'form' case. The resident then deletes it in the app (it was a double submission or a test). Later the owner re-imports the workbook from Admin -> Advanced -> Import, for example as the drift-check fix for 'missing rows'.
(b) The same, except the resident corrects the case's date in the app instead of deleting it.
(c) The resident opens the app, so the case is picked up. They then edit the Form response. The inbox updates the case but keeps createdAt at the first submit time (form-inbox.js:94), while Google Forms moves the row's Timestamp to the edit time. Then the owner re-imports.
confirmed.consequence: In (a) the deleted case comes back as a source:'import' case on all of the resident's devices. The drift check then reads IN SYNC, so nobody notices the delete was undone. In (b) and (c) the resident ends up with 2 cases for 1 sheet row, and their counts and Totals go up by one. Every later re-import repeats this for any Form case deleted or redated since.
confirmed.fix:
1. In runImport, give importCases the importKeys of the rows that withoutFormCases dropped (the same route as `found` in c077455), so they go into imports/{rid}.keys. A row that has once matched a Form case is then never imported again, whatever happens to that case.
2. Match Form cases on the response second at the sheet's offset without requiring the same day. The time to the second already identifies the response.
3. Best: by default, skip rows whose sheet timestamp is after the inbox went live (14 Oct 2026), because the inbox owns those. Import them only when the owner ticks 'include rows the inbox missed', with the drift check listing which ones.
4. Correct the claim in the drift-check skill.
verifier_fix:
The proposed fixes are partly right. Fix 3 is the only one that covers all three scenarios on its own, so make it the main fix: by default, skip sheet rows whose Timestamp is after the inbox went live, and import them only when the owner opts in, with the drift check listing which rows. It also covers a related case: a response imported before go-live and edited afterwards. Its Timestamp and content change, so its importKey changes too, and today both the re-import and the inbox's isImportOf would add it again.

Fix 1 (record the keys of dropped rows) protects only rows that were matched by an earlier import while their Form case was still unchanged. A case deleted or redated before any re-import is still brought back.

Fix 2 (drop the same-day requirement) fixes (b) but not (c), because the Form case's createdAt stays at the first submit. For (c) the inbox also needs to keep the latest submittedAt on the case (for example a formAt field) and have withoutFormCases match against both createdAt and formAt.

For (a), no browser-side matching can help, because the app owner can't read bins. Only fix 3, or a resident-side tombstone the import can read, prevents it.

Fix 4: correct the drift-check skill's claim that rows already in the app or its bin are skipped.

confirmed.title: A Case-tab row changed after import gets a new content-hash importKey, so the next re-import adds a second copy (or brings back one the resident deleted)
confirmed.scenario:
1. Rows from the old workbook are imported (imp_<hash#n>). The resident edits some of them in the app.
2. The Case row changes in the sheet. Ways this happens: the owner hand-fixes a row (e.g. syncing a resident's app text edits into the sheet); a category or date is fixed on the sheet side; or a response is edited on the Form before the inbox existed, which rewrites the row's text and Timestamp.
3. Later the owner re-imports the workbook for any reason. runImport always processes every row of every resident in the file.
confirmed.consequence: Each changed row hashes to a new key and a new doc id that is not in imports/{rid}.keys and not in `have`. It is written as a second case beside the resident's own copy. Each such row becomes a duplicate on the next re-import, so the resident's app counts run higher than the sheet's Totals. If the resident had deleted the original, the edited row brings it back. The drift skill already says that a sheet-side edit 'shows as a missing and an extra row', and its documented fix (re-import) is exactly what makes the duplicate.
confirmed.fix: Identify rows that have a Timestamp by (rid, timestamp to the second), not by content. When importCases writes a row, also record its timestamp second in imports/{rid} (for example a `stamps` array). Before writing a fresh row, check whether that rid already has an imported row with the same second, recorded or present as a source:'import' case with the same createdAt second. If so, don't write it; list it as 'changed in the sheet since import' for the owner to sort out. Keep the content hash only for the ~3,200 old rows with a blank Timestamp. As a one-off, add the keys of the 72 rows from 14 Oct to imports/{rid}.
verifier_fix:
The proposed direction is right: use (rid, timestamp second) as the identity of rows that have a Timestamp, record those stamps, and list changed rows for the owner instead of writing them. Refine it in four ways:

(1) Compare timestamps with tolerance. Compare a row's timestamp to existing source:'import' cases' createdAt with form-inbox's sameResponse() (same rid and date, a whole number of quarter-hours apart, ±1 s), not exact equality. The xlsx route stores the zoneless SGT stamp read as UTC, while other routes, such as Firetop's 72 rows on 14 Oct, may store the true UTC moment. Keep the recorded `stamps` in the parser's own convention.

(2) Handle Form edits. Google Forms moves the row's Timestamp to the edit time when a response is edited, so (rid, ts) cannot catch Form-edited rows. For post-inbox responses, have mergeFormEntries store the latest submittedAt on the case (e.g. `formAt`) and make withoutFormCases also match row.createdAt against formAt. Separately, the inbox has a sibling problem: isImportOf compares against the edit-time submittedAt, so a pre-inbox imported response edited on the Form becomes a second (form) case.

(3) Keep the content-hash keys. Still record them, and check them first, so existing imports/{rid} records keep working. Fall back to content-hash + #n only when the Timestamp is blank or when two real rows for one rid share a second.

(4) Fix the UI. Make the Admin UI (and Firetop's script) show 'changed in the sheet since import' and 'would be new' counts before writing, and drop the 'safe to run again' wording until this is in.

Backfill imports/{rid}.keys/stamps for the 14 Oct rows as proposed.

confirmed.title: Editing an old (workbook-imported) Form response now adds a second case through the inbox
confirmed.scenario:
1. A response sent before the inbox existed is in the app as an imported case. Its createdAt is the original sheet Timestamp, read +8 h.
2. 'Allow response editing' stays ON (the owner's decision of 14 Oct). The resident opens the edit link for that old response and fixes a category or typo.
3. Code.gs sends an inbox entry whose submittedAt is response.getTimestamp(), which is now the edit time.
4. On the next app open, mergeFormEntries finds no form case with that id. isImportOf compares the imported case's original time with the edit time, finds no match, and saves a new 'form' case.
confirmed.consequence: The resident has 2 cases for 1 sheet row (the old imported text plus the edited Form text), so app counts are higher than the sheet's. The next workbook re-import can't fix it, because withoutFormCases drops the edited row against the new Form case, so both copies stay. No toast or warning mentions a duplicate.
confirmed.fix: When an inbox entry has no form case and its submittedAt is after the inbox went live, look for a source:'import' case of that resident with the same date and the same initials, created before go-live. If there is one, treat the entry as an edit of that response. Either update that case in place (when its updatedAt shows no app edit since the import) or keep it and report 'edited Form response left as you changed it here', as the existing `kept` path does. Do not add a new case. Alternatively, have Code.gs flag edits: store the response ids it has seen in Script properties and mark an entry as an edit when its id was already there or the response is older than the install date. The app can then do the same lookup.
verifier_fix:
Use an exact first-submit signal instead of matching on date and initials.

1. **Code.gs sends the first-submit time as `firstAt`.** Either:
   - (a) read it from the Forms REST API (`GET https://forms.googleapis.com/v1/forms/{formId}/responses/{id}` with ScriptApp.getOAuthToken(); use `createTime`, the first submission, as opposed to `lastSubmittedTime`). Or:
   - (b) run a one-time snapshot now of {responseId: getTimestamp()} for every existing response, kept in a Drive file or chunked Script properties, and send `firstAt` from it whenever a snapshotted id is resubmitted.

   Add `firstAt` as an optional integer to `validFormEntry` in `logbook/firestore.rules`. That is a rules change: run `tools/test-rules.sh` first.

2. **The app matches on `firstAt`.** In form-inbox.js, `isImportOf` should use `sameResponse(c.createdAt, e.firstAt ?? e.submittedAt)`. When that matches and `firstAt !== submittedAt` (an edit of an imported response), do not add a case:
   - update the import case in place (keep its id, set source/importKey so later edits find it) if it has not been edited in the app since the import;
   - otherwise put it in `kept`, which shows the existing "left as you changed it here" toast.

3. **Fix the mirror path (re-import after a Form edit).** Store each form case's latest submittedAt, for example `importKey` `form:<id>@<written>#<submittedAt>` or a separate field. Make `withoutFormCases` match the sheet row's timestamp against both the case's createdAt and that latest submittedAt. Otherwise a re-import after any Form edit of an inbox-made case writes a duplicate import copy.

4. **Add unit tests:** an edited imported response (`firstAt` set) gives no new case, and a re-import after a Form edit drops the row.

confirmed.title: Matching on any whole quarter-hour offset mistakes a different response for the same one: the inbox silently deletes a new case, or a re-import never brings in a missing row
confirmed.scenario:
1. A resident has an imported case (from a re-import of rows the inbox missed, or the 14 Oct rows) for date D.
2. They send another Form response for date D. Its submit time differs from the imported row's sheet time by (k x 15 min - 8 h) +/- 1 s, anywhere within roughly -6 h to +22 h.
3. On pick-up, isImportOf treats it as the imported response. It goes into out.dupes, is pushed to out.done, and commitFormPickup deletes the inbox entry with case:null.
The mirror case: during a re-import, withoutFormCases drops a missing row because a different Form case on the same day lines up with it in the same way.
confirmed.consequence: In the first direction a resident's new case disappears with no message: pickupMessage ignores dupes, and the entry is gone from formInbox. It comes back only after the drift check shows a missing row and the owner re-imports. In the other direction the drift can't be fixed by re-importing, because the same row is dropped every time. Any two different responses of the same resident within 22 h of each other on the same case date have about a 1 in 300 chance of this.
confirmed.fix: Accept only the offsets that really occur, as a constant: `const SHEET_OFFSETS = [8 * 3600, 0]`, and match when `SHEET_OFFSETS.some(o => Math.abs(d - o) <= 1)`. That cuts false matches by about 28 to 57 times. For more safety, also require the same initials (or details), not just the same date, before treating an entry as a dupe.
verifier_fix:
The offsets part is right: `const SHEET_OFFSETS = [8 * 3600, 0]; return SHEET_OFFSETS.some(o => Math.abs(d - o) <= 1);`. In the repro it cuts the false-match rate from 0.33% to about 0.006%.

Also change logbook/test/form-inbox.test.mjs line 90 (5.5 h now expected false). Add regression tests:
- an entry 15 min / 2 h 15 min after an imported same-day row must be saved, not marked as a dupe;
- withoutFormCases must keep a row 30 min from a Form case.

Drop the extra "also require the same initials or details" check. It would break the real matches it exists for:
- a Form case or import case the resident edited in the app;
- an edited Form response.
Both would no longer match, so the case would be counted twice: imported again on a re-import, or picked up again from the inbox. If more safety is wanted, compare categories only as a tie-breaker when more than one candidate matches, never as a requirement.
